Three distinct income measures are kept separate and must not be interchanged: T12 historical (EGI 691,200 / NOI before reserves 320,000 / NCF 305,600 for Sep-2025 through Aug-2026), current contractual rent roll (56,025/month = 672,300 annualized at 2026-08-31), and the supplied underwriting scenario (EGI 1,025,280 / NOI 647,395.20 / NCF 631,795.20 for Sep-2026 forward).

The underwriting plan is the owner/scenario plan, not a lender-approved forecast (Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1). Underwritten NOI of 647,395.20 is 2.02x T12 NOI of 320,000; underwritten NCF is 2.07x T12 NCF. All sizing above is therefore conditional on the supplied scenario being accepted by credit.

Reconciliation, gross potential rent: rent-roll total potential (56,025 occupied + 15 vacant units x 2,025 market = 30,375) = 86,400/month = 1,036,800/year, which ties exactly to T12 annual GPR of 1,036,800 (T12-Statement.pdf p.2). Underwritten GPR of 1,056,000 is 19,200 (+1.85%) above both, and is a supplied scenario figure, expressly 'not inferred from the T12'.

Reconciliation, revenue loss: T12 actual loss (vacancy 302,400 + concessions 64,800 + bad debt 8,400 = 375,600) is 36.23% of T12 GPR. The underwriting plan applies a 7.00% combined loss (73,920). This implies stabilization from 68.75% physical occupancy by count (61.81% by area) to roughly 93% economic occupancy, i.e., lease-up of the 15 vacant 1,100 SF units. No lease-up schedule, downtime, concession or leasing-cost budget is supplied for that gap. This is the single largest driver of the sized loan and the principal unresolved underwriting item.
Reconciliation, other income: T12 actual other income/recoveries is 30,000; the plan underwrites 43,200 (+13,200 / +44.0%) with no supporting detail in the packet.

Reconciliation, reserves: T12 actual reserves 14,400 (300/unit) versus underwritten 15,600 (325/unit x 48). Capital improvements of 184,000, loan P&I of 294,000 and depreciation of 180,000 in the T12 are below-the-line per the statement footnote and Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1 and are excluded from operating expense.

The T12 statement prints no NOI subtotal. Per Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1, an accounting package may label cash flow after reserves as 'property NOI'; NOI before reserves (320,000) and NCF after reserves (305,600) are stated separately above to avoid that conflation.

Rate distinction: the 6.25% contract rate governs actual payments; the 6.50% sizing rate (floor) governs the LTV/DSCR/debt-yield test. First-year contractual debt service is interest-only at 6.25% (400,468.09), which is 85,528.22 less than the 485,996.31 amortizing sizing debt service. Actual first-year coverage on underwritten NCF is 631,795.20/400,468.09 = 1.58x, but this is an IO-period artifact and reverts on the month-37 amortization step-up.

Structural note: amortization is 30 years while maturity is 60 months, and the first 36 months are interest-only. The loan therefore matures with a balloon at approximately the original principal less only 24 months of amortization; no refinancing takeout, extension option, cash sweep, earn-out, holdback, interest reserve or fee capitalization is assumed (Lender-Terms.pdf p.1).

Insurance evidence caveat: the $45,600 figure is a dated insurer renewal confirmation as represented inside Property-and-Plan.pdf p.2 ('renewal confirmation dated August 25, 2026'), not a scenario allowance, and is reported as verified on that basis. The underlying insurer document is not itself included in the packet, so credit should condition on receipt of the binder/quote. If credit declines to treat the plan's representation as verification, verified_renewal_insurance would be unknown and the T12 actual of 40,800 would be the only observed premium.

summary: Cedar Landing (48 units, 43,200 SF, San Antonio TX; fictional) as of 2026-08-31 is 68.75% occupied by count and 61.81% by area, with 33 occupied units producing $56,025 of monthly contractual base rent ($672,300 annualized). The T12 for Sep-2025 through Aug-2026 shows EGI of $691,200, operating expenses of $371,200, NOI before reserves of $320,000, reserves of $14,400 and NCF of $305,600; the statement prints no NOI subtotal, and capex ($184,000), P&I ($294,000) and depreciation ($180,000) are below the line. The supplied underwriting scenario is materially more aggressive: GPR $1,056,000 less a 7.00% combined revenue loss plus $43,200 other income gives EGI of $1,025,280; a lender-normalized management fee of $35,884.80 (3.50% of EGI, above the $28,000 T12 actual) brings operating expenses to $377,884.80, producing NOI before reserves of $647,395.20, reserves of $15,600 ($325 x 48) and NCF of $631,795.20 - roughly double the T12, driven almost entirely by an unscheduled lease-up of the 15 vacant 1,100 SF units. Capitalizing underwritten NOI at the lender's 5.75% rate gives an indicative value of $11,258,177. Sizing at the 6.50% floor rate (above the 6.25% contract rate) with a 30-year monthly amortizing constant of 0.0758482 yields limits of $6,754,906 (60% LTV), $6,407,489 (1.30x DSCR on NCF) and $7,019,947 (9.00% debt yield on NCF); DSCR binds at a maximum loan of $6,407,489, with sizing debt service of $485,996, DSCR of exactly 1.30x and debt yield of 9.86%. First-year contractual debt service is interest-only at the 6.25% contract rate, $400,468 ($33,372/month), $85,528 below the sizing figure, so reported first-year coverage of 1.58x is an IO artifact that reverts at month 37 against a 60-month maturity and a near-full balloon. Net proceeds to the borrower are $1,778,415 after the $4,500,000 payoff, $64,075 origination fee (1.00%) and $65,000 fixed closing costs - a cash-out result, contingent on credit accepting the scenario. The specified downside is punishing: EGI -5% with management recomputed to $34,091 cuts NOI to $597,925 and NCF to $582,325, and adding +100 bps to the sizing rate (7.50%, constant 0.0839056) drops the maximum loan to $5,338,648 (DSCR still binding) - a $1,068,842 or 16.7% reduction that would leave proceeds roughly $1.07mm short of the base case while still covering the payoff. On unit 101, the executed lease governs: $1,575 per month, expiry 2027-06-30, $1,200 deposit (not income); the conditional renewal option shows no exercise notice, acknowledgment or amendment in the packet, so the expiry is not extended. Every occupied lease rolls between 2026-09-30 and 2027-08-31. Insurance is underwritten at $45,600 per a renewal confirmation dated 2026-08-25 as represented in the plan (versus $40,800 T12 actual), subject to receipt of the binder itself. Prepayment friction is 1% of outstanding principal in years 1-2 (about $64,075 on the sized loan, unamortized during IO) with no stated penalty thereafter and no swap or breakage exposure. Indicated internal recommendation: the request is financeable at up to $6,407,489 on the supplied scenario, but the proceeds are governed by an unproven lease-up rather than in-place cash flow - T12 NCF of $305,600 would only support roughly $3.10mm at the same 1.30x DSCR test - so approval should be conditioned on an appraisal, insurance binder, lease and deposit audit, a documented lease-up plan with leasing-cost budget, and consideration of an earn-out or holdback structure rather than full funding at close.
